editorial:
You follow Bart Millard as he rides the high of “I Can Only Imagine,” filling arenas while trying to be the husband and father his past never taught him to be. The story keeps one foot in the spotlight and one in the quiet rooms where old wounds still sting, especially with his son Sam. When Tim Timmons joins MercyMe for a major tour, his easy warmth and gratitude give Bart a new mirror, but Tim’s hidden struggles keep the drama from feeling too easy. The tone stays heartfelt and family-focused, with music woven into the emotions rather than just playing in the background.

The acting feels sincere, the concert scenes have real energy, and the family conflict gives the movie a steady heartbeat. It can lean into familiar faith-drama beats, and some emotional turns arrive a little neatly, but the central relationships keep you invested. If you enjoy uplifting music stories about forgiveness, second chances, and parents learning to listen, this is a good pick. Stream it in 4K Ultra HD on Prime Video, rent it on Apple TV, or grab the 4K Blu-ray for the best sound and picture.
endingExplained: In the final stretch, Bart stops running from his past and opens up to Sam and Shannon, choosing family over the tour’s pressure. Tim’s secret comes into the light as a hidden health struggle, and instead of pushing him away, Bart and the band rally around him. The last scenes bring the family and Tim together on stage, turning the final performance into a moment of forgiveness, gratitude, and renewed purpose.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves uplifting music stories about forgiveness and family.
